title: Vessel-Simmered Fermented Algerian Lamb Tagine
description: A rich and flavorful Algerian dish featuring fermented lamb, szechuan peppercorns, and a sweet and crisp finish. Best served with crusty bread or couscous.
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together kosher salt, black peppercorns, szechuan peppercorns, and coriander seeds.
Rub the spice mixture all over the lamb shoulder, making sure to coat it evenly.
Place the lamb in a large iron teppan vessel or Dutch oven, fat side up.
Heat the olive oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the lamb in the skillet for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until browned.
Transfer the lamb to the teppan vessel, and add the lamb or beef broth.
Bring the broth to a boil, then cover the vessel and transfer it to a preheated oven at 300°F (150°C).
Braise the lamb for 2 1/2 hours, or until tender and easily shredded with a fork.
Remove the lamb from the vessel, and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before slicing it thinly.
Strain the cooking liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, discarding the solids.
Skim off any excess fat from the surface of the liquid, and let it cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate the liquid overnight, or for at least 8 hours, to allow it to ferment and thicken.
